Simulation study, built from commit f167fd3 (2026-10-05) of the project repository. Every number is read from its result files (see Number provenance).

Report Supplementary material: S1 Supplementary text S2 Adult reference benchmarks S3 Realistic adult comparison S4 Smaller heads S5 Simulated interictal spikes and head motion S6 Methods, uncertainty and limitations S7 Parameters, provenance and assumptions S8 Number provenance S9 Reproduce and download Project summary by milestone

S8. Number provenance

Every number in the report and in its supplementary text (S1) is a named fact, inserted into the text when the site is built. scripts/report_facts.py collects the facts of its modules (scripts/report_facts_*.py), which read or derive each value from the committed result files and record its source: the result file and the key path in it, or how the value is derived. Both documents refer to each fact by name; a reference to a missing fact fails the build.

The report uses 597 and the supplementary text 2,203 of the 62,951 facts available (2,478 different facts, 322 of them in both), listed below in order of first use, the report's first; the last column names the documents that use each.

Data sources. The pediatric facts derive from results of the infant templates and the school-aged children. Infant templates: O'Reilly et al. (2021), built from the Neurodevelopmental MRI Database (Richards et al. 2016). Children A-C: OpenNeuro ds005234 v2.2.0 (doi:10.18112/openneuro.ds005234.v2.2.0; Fadeev et al. 2024).
